profile.primary_purpose: Introduce the research lab, communicate vision and mission, and drive user sign-ups to explore AI image generation tools
profile.brand_signature: Deep navy and dark blue backgrounds create an immersive, almost cosmic atmosphere reminiscent of digital code or a night sky. The monospace typography and matrix-like text animation in the hero convey technical sophistication while ethereal cyan-blue imagery of anatomical forms suggests the intersection of technology and humanity.

visual_language.accent_strategy: Subtle colored accents (emerald, yellow, rose, violet) differentiate CTAs and section headers against the dark blue canvas, creating visual hierarchy without overwhelming the contemplative aesthetic.
visual_language.highlights: Cyan-tinted X-ray style imagery of human anatomy creates visual intrigue, with hover states revealing project descriptions through dark overlays

target_audience: Creative professionals and artists seeking AI-powered image generation tools to enhance their creative workflow
Technology enthusiasts and early adopters interested in cutting-edge generative AI research and experimentation
Researchers and developers exploring the intersection of AI, creativity, and human expression
Community-minded individuals who value being part of a research-driven movement exploring the future of human creativity
strategy.executive_synthesis: Midjourney's visual identity deliberately balances technical sophistication with humanistic warmth to position itself as more than a tool—a research community exploring humanity's creative future. The dark, immersive interface with code-like animations signals technical prowess while ethereal anatomical imagery (eyes, hearts, brains, hands) grounds the technology in human experience. This visual strategy supports their positioning as a 'community-funded research lab' rather than a typical SaaS product, attracting users who want to participate in a philosophical journey about creativity and AI, not just consume a service.

style_classification.reasoning: The screenshot reveals a distinctly Cyberpunk aesthetic with its deep navy/black background (#06051D) serving as the canvas for luminous cyan/electric blue (#63B3ED) accent colors - the quintessential "neon on dark" Cyberpunk signature. The hero section features a cascading matrix of code/text characters creating a digital rain effect reminiscent of classic cyberpunk imagery, reinforcing the high-tech atmosphere. The monospace typography (JetBrains Mono) throughout the entire site - from headers to body text - directly evokes terminal/coding interfaces, a core Cyberpunk design element. The project images showcase glossy 3D renders of anatomical and abstract forms (eyes, brains, hearts, heads) in monochromatic blue with dramatic lighting, suggesting a futuristic, technological interpretation of human elements - fitting the "high tech" aspect of Cyberpunk. The layout is grid-based strict with centered symmetric organization, matching Cyberpunk's structured digital interface aesthetic. Glass blur effects (backdrop-blur) on buttons and panels add the layered, interface-like quality common to Cyberpunk UI.
style_classification.reasoning_secondary: The surface profile explicitly identifies glass_blur as a texture classification, and the design consistently employs frosted glass effects throughout the UI. Navigation buttons use backdrop-blur-md with semi-transparent colored backgrounds (emerald-900/20, yellow-900/20, etc.). The language button features bg-[#060522]/40 with backdrop-blur-md and border-white/10. All interactive cards have subtle white border overlays (border-white/10 hover:border-white/20) creating glow effects. The rounded button shapes with soft shadows and translucent panels floating over the dark background demonstrate classic Glassmorphism layered transparency. This secondary style complements the Cyberpunk primary by adding a modern, polished interface quality to the raw digital aesthetic.

layout.section_separation: Sections are separated by generous vertical whitespace (4rem/64px gaps between sections) on a consistent dark navy background (#06051d). No alternating backgrounds or divider lines; separation is achieved purely through whitespace rhythm and color-coded section icons (violet, blue, emerald, yellow) that create visual punctuation points.

insights: Minimal centered layout with max-width constraint (896px/4xl) creates a narrow reading column that emphasizes vertical rhythm and generous breathing room around content
Color-coded iconography system (violet for About, blue for Projects, emerald for Careers, yellow for Contact) creates visual hierarchy and section differentiation without heavy graphical elements
Interactive project cards use subtle hover transforms (scale 1.03, shadow-2xl) and black/60 overlay with text reveal to create depth and engagement within the monochromatic blue palette
Consistent use of backdrop-blur, semi-transparent backgrounds (e.g., bg-[#060522]/40), and subtle white/10 borders creates a layered glassmorphism aesthetic throughout UI elements

rules.description: Serves as the primary dark surface and structural backbone of the design, providing a high-contrast canvas.
Acts as the primary action and highlight color, drawing attention to interactive elements against the dark canvas.
Provides low-contrast structural support and legible secondary text styling against the deep dark backgrounds.
Adds warmth and depth as a secondary dark background, creating visual hierarchy and section separation from the primary navy.

insights: The palette relies on an ultra-dark primary background (#06051D) to allow the luminous electric blue (#63B3ED) to pop as a highly visible accent.
A shift from cool dark navy to a deep plum (#2D0E36) provides subtle, warm thematic variation in dark surfaces without relying on flat grays.
The reliance on muted slate (#CAD5E2) for secondary elements ensures UI components remain visible but secondary to the vibrant interactive blue.

paragraphs.description: Body are used for longer passages of text in your app. Use typefaces intended for body styles, which are readable at smaller sizes and can be comfortably read in longer passages.

labels.description: Label styles are smaller, utilitarian styles, used for things like the text inside components or for very small text in the content body, such as captions.

others.description: Font that does not have a classifier, that is small like regular.

typography.highlights: Text treatments are minimal, relying primarily on standard underlines with offset (`underline-offset-2`) and color shifts for links.
insights: Unconventional use of monospace (JetBrains Mono) for primary headings and body copy, giving the site a distinct technical and developer-oriented identity.
DM Sans (a sans-serif) is reserved specifically for interactive top-level navigation buttons, drawing clear distinction between UI controls and content.
Typography relies on standard weights (400 for text, 500 for cards, 700 for buttons) combined with precise line heights (e.g., `leading-relaxed` for long-form text, `leading-tight` for cards).
